title: Characteristic ideal of the fine Selmer group and results on $Œº$-invariance under isogeny in the function field case

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper begins with an arbitrary one-variable function field K over a finite field, but then identifies its smooth projective curve as "C_K = P^1_F". This is false in general: a global function field is the function field of an arbitrary smooth projective geometrically integral curve, not necessarily the projective line. Later sections also treat finite extensions L/K, whose associated curves need not be P^1 either.

The displayed recursive definition is mathematically malformed: it states "1 = X", "t = X^p+tX", "t^n=t)" and treats polynomials in F[t] as though they themselves were additive Carlitz polynomials. The intended identities presumably concern Carlitz actions [1](X)=X and [t](X)=tX+X^p, but the text as written does not define [P(t)](X). Consequently the subsequent torsion-field construction is unsupported. The asserted Galois group "Z_p^N × (F[t]/P)^×" is also not the standard pro-p factor; for a prime P of degree d, the pro-p part of the P-adic unit group has finite Z_p-rank d, not countably infinite rank Z_p^N.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 2.4, definition of Φ_0 and of the functor G
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper defines Φ_n=ω_n/ω_{n-1} for n≥1 and then writes "Φ_0 = X". Here X is not the Iwasawa-algebra element corresponding to Φ_0; earlier the Iwasawa variable is T and ω_0=T. This makes later formulas involving Φ_0 ill-defined. In addition, the displayed definition "G := lim_n (X/ω_nX[p^∞])" omits the argument of the functor and is syntactically ambiguous.

Both inequalities are stated for H^1(G,B): "|H^1(G,B)| ≤ |B|^d" and again "|H^1(G,B)| ≤ |B|^{d(d-1)/2}". The cited standard result bounds H^1 by |B|^d and H^2 by |B|^{d(d-1)/2}; the second occurrence must be H^2, not H^1. As written the second asserted H^1 bound is generally unjustified and can be stronger than the first.

The proof says that (ii) "follows from (i), via the structure theorem." This does not follow. A finitely generated torsion Λ-module with μ=0 and characteristic ideal coprime to every ω_n can still have unbounded quotients X/p^nX; e.g. X=Λ/(T-p) is isomorphic to Z_p as a Z_p-module, has μ=0 and characteristic ideal coprime to all ω_n, but |X/p^nX|=p^n is unbounded. Thus the claimed uniform boundedness requires an additional argument or hypothesis.

The proof explicitly asserts "0 = (A(L_n) ⊗ Q_p/Z_p)_div". This is false whenever A(L_n) has positive Mordell-Weil rank: if A(L_n) contains Z^r, then A(L_n)⊗Q_p/Z_p contains (Q_p/Z_p)^r and is itself divisible. The claimed exact sequence and the conclusion G((A(L∞)⊗Q_p/Z_p)^∨)=0 therefore do not follow from the given argument.

predicted_errors.error_location: Theorem 1.1 and Proposition 4.6 / Theorem 4.9 characteristic-ideal formulas
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The product is indexed by n≥0 but its exponent is defined as e_n=(rank E(L_n)-rank E(L_{n-1}))/φ(p^n). Neither L_{-1} nor e_0 is defined. Elsewhere (Remark 3.6) the same rank-difference expression is explicitly stated only for n≥1. Since Φ_0 is included in the product, the main formula is not well-defined as stated.

Immediately after stating Theorem 4.9, the text labelled "Proof" does not prove the theorem about the characteristic ideal of R^S. Instead it abruptly introduces two isogenous curves E_1,E_2, maps λ_i, and diagrams involving ordinary Selmer groups—material belonging to Theorem 5.1. No argument is given that finite fine Tate-Shafarevich group transfers the Proposition 4.6 formula from the fine Mordell-Weil group to R^S. Thus the central theorem is unsupported in the submitted text.

Theorem 1.6 and the surrounding discussion impose H^2_fl(K∞,E_i[p∞])=0. Theorem 5.1 as actually stated instead assumes H^1_fl(K∞,E_i[p∞])=0. Its proof repeatedly uses H^2_fl(K∞,E_i[p∞])=0, for example to deduce H^1(Γ,H^1_fl(K∞,E_i[p∞]))=0 and to derive equation (11). Therefore the theorem statement does not contain the hypothesis used by its proof and contradicts the introduction.

predicted_errors.error_location: Theorem 5.1 proof, local-term argument following equation (10)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The proof states that because K∞ is unramified, "Gal(K_{∞,w}/K_{∞,w}) ≅ ∏_{ℓ≠p} Z_ℓ" and hence ker(f_4)=coker(f_4)=0. The displayed Galois group has the same field in numerator and denominator and is therefore trivial, not the indicated product. If an absolute local Galois group was intended, it is not ∏_{ℓ≠p} Z_ℓ (in characteristic p it has a nontrivial wild pro-p part). Hence the asserted vanishing of the local maps is not established.

The remark says that for the purely inseparable Frobenius isogeny, "the order of the kernel of isogeny equals its separable degree," and concludes that the μ-invariants are equal. For an isogeny of elliptic curves, the finite kernel group scheme has rank equal to the full degree, not merely the separable degree. A purely inseparable Frobenius has a nontrivial finite flat kernel (e.g. of rank q), even though it has only one geometric point. Since the paper's p-primary arguments use flat cohomology and finite flat group schemes, replacing the kernel by its geometric-point order is invalid.

K∞ is defined as the full trivializing extension K(E[ℓ∞]), whose Galois group is stated to be an open subgroup of GL_2(Z_ℓ). Theorem 1.5 and Theorem 6.3 then assume that this same G=Gal(K∞/K) is pro-p, with p≠ℓ. A full ℓ-adic torsion-field extension has an infinite pro-ℓ congruence component and cannot be pro-p. Passing to an open pro-ℓ subgroup would require changing the extension, not merely adding the stated assumption. Thus the main noncommutative theorem is formulated for an incompatible/vacuous setup.

predicted_errors.error_location: Appendix A, use of μ and Euler characteristics in the ℓ≠p case
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Although the appendix concerns ℓ-primary Selmer groups with ℓ≠p, it repeatedly invokes Definition 2.14 and Corollary 2.17 using p-primary torsion and writes that one should calculate the "logarithm to the p-base" of Euler characteristics. The relevant Iwasawa μ-invariant and valuations in the ℓ-adic setting must be defined using ℓ, not the characteristic p. No replacement of p by ℓ is made. Consequently the claimed μ-comparisons do not follow from the cited p-adic statements as written.

predicted_errors.error_location: Appendix A, diagram (13) and proof of Theorem A.1
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Diagram (13) is said to concern an extension 𝒦, but its rows are written with S(E_i/K), rather than S(E_i/𝒦). The diagram labels its vertical maps g_i, while the proof immediately analyzes ker(f_1), coker(f_1), and later refers to an undefined "equation (A)" and to f_2. These are not merely cosmetic: the snake-lemma sequence and ensuing Euler-characteristic calculation are for unspecified maps, so the proof does not establish Theorem A.1.
